title: AI Agent Gateway: Open-source tool keeps credentials out of agent configs
key_facts: Tuskira released AI Agent Gateway as open source; it sits between AI agents and the MCP tool servers and model providers they call.
It runs in the user's own environment without a Tuskira account.
The gateway checks a key and profile on every call, blocks denied calls and attaches the real credential from an encrypted store, so the agent never holds the token.
A key with no profile attached lets the caller name its own profile, so a leaked unbound key can ask for any profile.
The demo stack stores LLM request and response bodies (up to 1 MiB each); one setting turns that off.
It runs on macOS and Linux; Windows through WSL2 is untested.
quote_evidence: An allowed call gets the real credential pulled from an encrypted store and attached on the way out, so the agent never holds the GitHub token.
A key with no profile attached lets the caller name its own profile in a request header, so a leaked unbound key can ask for any profile it wants.
why_it_matters_hint: Keeps passwords and keys out of the config files of every developer laptop and build server.
notes: Help Net Security describes the vendor's own product; no independent test reported.
